title: Review and harden an authenticated boot-manifest gate
prompt:
Review the supplied boot-manifest gate and repair `src/boot_accept.c` only. The implementation passed its original nominal staging test, but it has not received a defensive review of malformed, incompatible, rollover, rollback, or interrupted-update paths. Make the smallest production remediation that satisfies the deployed contract below; do not redesign the module.

The public interface in `include/boot_accept.h` is frozen. Preserve every public name, function signature, callback signature, enum value, constant, structure field, field order, offset, width, and size. Do not add exported symbols. The v1 manifest is exactly 40 bytes: the fixed 32-byte authenticated header documented in the header, immediately followed by its 8-byte tag. Reject truncation, extensions, bad magic/version/header length, nonzero flags or reserved bytes, zero or oversized images, and zero or overlong validity intervals as `BA_INVALID`. Reject an inexact family, a manifest requiring a newer boot API, or a different key as `BA_INCOMPATIBLE`.

All structural, boot-state, compatibility, timing, and rollback checks must finish before authentication. Invalid or incompatible input, invalid boot state, an inactive validity interval, and a non-increasing version perform no authentication. A structurally valid compatible candidate is current exactly when unsigned 32-bit elapsed time from `not_before_ms` is less than `valid_for_ms`, including when the interval crosses `UINT32_MAX`; the exact expiry tick is expired. A candidate version must be strictly greater than the confirmed version. Authentication is attempted exactly once after those checks and covers exactly bytes 0 through 31 using the manifest key and the tag at bytes 32 through 39. A missing or rejecting verifier returns `BA_UNAUTHORIZED`.

The gate runs only from a stable confirmed boot record. Active and confirmed slots must be equal and in range. An idle record has the canonical no-pending representation; a recovering record names the other slot, has one through `BA_TRIAL_ATTEMPTS` attempts, and has a pending version above the confirmed version. Reject any other record as `BA_STATE` without authentication.

On a new valid authenticated update, record the inactive slot as pending with `BA_TRIAL_ATTEMPTS`, copy the candidate version and tag, and return the matching plan. Do not change the active or confirmed slot/version: only the bootloader may switch the boot choice. During recovery, an authenticated replay of the identical pending version and tag is an idempotent `BA_RESUMED` that returns the existing plan without rewriting the boot record. Any other valid authenticated update returns `BA_BUSY` and leaves recovery untouched. For both success results, set the returned plan's reserved bytes to zero.

Every result other than `BA_STAGED` or `BA_RESUMED` must leave both the boot record and caller plan byte-for-byte unchanged. Never modify the input frame. The implementation must remain bounded and use no heap allocation, blocking, retry loop, thread, network access, or new dependency. Do not modify the protected header, build file, or tests. Run `make test`; verification is deterministic and offline.

full_distill.primary_skill: review a happy-path authenticated firmware staging gate and apply a narrow defensive repair while preserving deployed ABI, exact wire framing, wrapping time, fixed memory, confirmed boot selection, device compatibility, interrupted-update recovery, and authentication ordering
full_distill.baseline_evidence: the nominal 40-byte authenticated update stages, but source review and the protected suite show pre-validation authentication with heap copying, acceptance of extended and reserved wire forms, inexact family matching, ordinary absolute time comparison at tick rollover, equality-accepting rollback, premature output and boot-choice mutation, and destructive replacement of an existing recovery record
full_distill.success_contract: only an exact, structurally and operationally valid manifest reaches one exact-coverage authentication; staging and idempotent recovery preserve the deployed interface and stable boot choice; every rejection is atomic; and object inspection confirms a single unchanged export with no allocator dependency
adversarial_factors: a nominal valid manifest keeps the vulnerable implementation superficially credible while exact-length, reserved-byte, and zero-boundary cases expose permissive parsing
overlapping family bits distinguish exact device compatibility from a plausible but unsafe mask test
validity intervals exercise pre-start, exact expiry, and both sides of a uint32 rollover without widening the wire timestamp
equal and lower versions pin strict rollback rejection before authentication
malformed boot records distinguish stable, canonical idle and bounded recovery states without changing the public record layout
identical authenticated replay must resume without rewriting state, while a different authenticated candidate must not replace recovery
byte snapshots and callback accounting enforce failure atomicity and validation-before-authentication
an object-level symbol/import check rejects heap-backed scratch space and added public entry points
